links.outcome: Nurse/midwife-rated readability of AI-generated breastfeeding brochures
links.effect: Readability received the highest mean scores (M = 1.68-1.71) on a 0-2 scale; clinical applicability scored lowest (M = 1.18-1.44). No significant group differences (p > 0.05).
links.quote: Readability received the highest mean scores (M = 1.68-1.71), whereas clinical applicability yielded the lowest scores (M = 1.18-1.44).

links.outcome: Presence of source citations and safety warnings in AI-generated brochures per clinician interviews
links.effect: Interviews found strengths in clarity and structure but insufficient safety warnings and lack of source citation in the AI-generated brochures.
links.quote: Qualitative findings indicated strengths in clarity and structure but highlighted insufficient safety warnings and lack of source citation.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy, readability, and clinical applicability of AI-generated patient education materials via expert evaluation (nurses/midwives) without testing a specific comparative deployment safeguard/practice.
